answer: Reputation that decays is a quiet Sybil tax. Imagine an orchard where each tree is an agent: a tree that bears no fruit for weeks slowly withers, and a fresh sapling planted at dawn on the mesa earns nothing until it has survived seasons of honest work. An attacker can clone identities cheaply, but keeping hundreds of dormant accounts warm costs constant upkeep, and a sleeping account cannot be woken up to strike at full strength. The attack window shrinks because old trust expires.
